assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system is a new drug modality: degrading rather than inhibiting a target. It is conceptually simple, chemically elegant and already a game-changer, with degraders in late-stage clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept; Ciulli supplied VHL ligands and structural, mechanistic rigor. The molecular-glue arm (Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Gray, Kim) is a competing credit stream and cannot fit in three, so I would anchor on the PROTAC pioneers.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of work, independent replication across many labs and targets, and clinical proof of concept; timely recognition.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should split PROTACs from thalidomide-type molecular-glue mechanism.
Regulatory approval of a PROTAC drug is not yet established, which some members may want first.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand breaks through engineered deaminase chemistry. It has been shown to work in cells and animals and has reached patients, and it is chemistry-driven protein engineering with real consequences.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the program; Komor (cytosine base editors) and Gaudelli (adenine base editors, including evolution of an adenine deaminase) were the decisive first authors. Kondo and Nishida's independent cytidine-deaminase work is a priority question that I cannot resolve from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Clinical use is emerging with first-patient results; early but substantial confirmation by many groups. Recognition is plausible now, though somewhat early.
uncertainties: Priority claim by Nishida and Kondo for a related cytidine-deaminase editor.
The CRISPR prize in 2020 may make the committee wary of another genome-editing prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics put electronic structure and nuclear motion on one footing, making ab initio dynamics practical. It changed how liquids, interfaces and reactions are simulated, and it connects quantitatively to experiment, my own standard for good theory.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is by exactly two people, so attribution is unusually clean and fits a prize. Parrinello's separate metadynamics and ML-potential work could be credited elsewhere, but here the pair is clear.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use and thorough independent validation; if anything, the work is overdue.
uncertainties: Computational methods have been honored in 1998 and 2013; the committee may feel the theory slot is filled.
Dependence on DFT accuracy limits quantitative predictions in some systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by chemistry on surfaces (reversible terminators and clustered amplification) made genome sequencing cheap and routine. Its consequences for biology and medicine are enormous and already realized.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the Solexa chemistry; Mayer co-invented clonal colony/cluster sequencing. Rothberg (454 pyrosequencing) and Ju are also credited, and the allocation among competing platforms is genuinely disputed.
assessment.maturity: Mature, broadly confirmed technology that has been in universal use for fifteen years; a long-delayed recognition.
uncertainties: Whether the chemistry achievement is judged distinct from Sanger's earlier prize.
Which of the several platforms and inventors deserves the credit, with only three places.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Orbitrap is a new type of mass analyzer that delivered high resolution and mass accuracy in a compact format. It became central to proteomics, metabolomics and small-molecule analysis, a clear game-changer for analytical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Single inventor on the supplied credit; the invention of the analyzer principle is credited to Makarov, though a Nobel would need to weigh the role of Cooks and others in related ion-trap physics, which I cannot assess from the list.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for over twenty years with extensive independent confirmation; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Prize with a single analytical-instrument laureate has limited recent precedent.
Possible allocation to proteomics users rather than instrument inventor, which I cannot resolve.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs allow site-specific incorporation of non-canonical amino acids in living cells, extending protein chemistry beyond the twenty natural building blocks. The method is a general platform for engineered proteins.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first in vivo eukaryotic and bacterial expansion; Chin extended to multiple codons, quadruplet codons and whole-organism genetic code reprogramming. Reasonable three-person configuration, though Yokoyama and Mehl are also credited.
assessment.maturity: Twenty years of use and replication; applications in drug conjugates and biologics are growing but still partial.
uncertainties: The 2018 directed-evolution prize may narrow the committee's interest in engineered biocatalysis.
Does the application impact match the conceptual novelty?

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single DNA and RNA molecules through current blockades, enabling long-read sequencing with portable devices. It is a clear new analytical principle that has become practical.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton and Deamer demonstrated the principle in 1996; Akeson showed processive enzyme-controlled movement; Bayley made the engineered pore. Allocation is difficult, and I cannot confirm from the supplied text the current status of every credited individual.
assessment.maturity: Commercial devices exist and are broadly validated, but accuracy for some applications is still improving.
uncertainties: Sharply contested attribution among five credited names with only three slots.
Whether the chemistry or the physics and engineering component dominates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers made efficient, cheaply processable solar cells within a few years, a remarkable and widely replicated rise in efficiency.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka's 2009 sensitized cells opened the field; Park's solid-state cell and Snaith's thin-film planar architecture drove the leap in efficiency. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also have substantive claims, so any three-person choice is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is remarkable but long-term operational stability and lead toxicity remain open, so the technology's maturity is questionable.
uncertainties: Device stability and commercial viability not yet demonstrated at scale.
Highly crowded credit among six names.
